methods.notes: Advertised name is "pix <12-hex-MAC>" (the app lowercases the name first; the regex above covers either case as seen on air). Scan filter is the 0100 service under either original base UUID; after connecting, pick the LEGACY base if the legacy 0100 service is present, else V1. The mini variant advertises 00000100-9552-4325-8021-a85f8136a5c4 instead.

device.name: Pix Backpack / Pix Mini
device.notes:
Wearable 16x20 RGB LED matrix sewn into a backpack (Kickstarter 2018, "Pix Backpack"; a smaller "Pix Mini" for kids followed in 2019), driven by the vendor's Pix app (Android package style.pix.app, v1.40 analyzed; minSdk 21, targetSdk 29). Vendor Pix Inc. (pix.style) appears defunct and the app is delisted from Google Play — this is an abandoned-hardware rescue. The app is a React Native build: all protocol logic is in its JavaScript bundle, the native side is stock RN boilerplate, and BLE goes through the stock react-native-ble-manager library (no custom native code, no vendor SDK).
LOCAL-ONLY VIABILITY: HIGH. Scan, connect, image/animation upload, brightness, scrolling text, clock/widgets and games are all pure local BLE. The app silently creates an anonymous cloud account, but that exists only for the content marketplace; sign-in is optional and nothing in the control path needs the cloud. Cloud endpoints in this build point at the vendor's STAGE environment (app.stage.pix.style, device-gateway .stage.pix.style) — production hostnames (app.pix.style, device-gateway.pix.style) presumably existed as siblings. Both are dead with the vendor; only the marketplace, news feed and firmware hosting are lost, and firmware hosting is replaceable (see OTA below).
IDENTIFICATION: the advertised local name is "pix <12 hex digits>" — the app lowercases the name, splits on spaces, requires the first word to be "pix" and the last word to match /^[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$/ (the 12 hex digits are the device MAC and double as its id). Scan filter is the 0100 service UUID under either of the two "original" base UUIDs:
  LEGACY  0000xxxx-e984-11e7-b78e-ffd6fcc3450f
  V1      0000xxxx-e984-11e7-b78e-ffd6fcc34510
After connecting, the protocol variant is chosen from the DISCOVERED services: if the legacy 0100 service is present the legacy base is used, otherwise V1. Both services below have identical characteristic layouts; only the UUID base differs. A third base (0000xxxx-9552-4325-8021-a85f8136a5c4) exists for the mini variant but is build-time disabled in the analyzed app — recorded under variants, never exercised.
TRANSPORT: one GATT service 0100 (per base above). Characteristic 0101 is the RPC channel (write only): every command is [callId u8, opcode u8, payload...] — callId is a per-command counter that wraps 255 -> 0. NO length field, NO checksum, NO crypto anywhere in the BLE path (the app's only crypto is MD5 for firmware integrity). The response characteristic is declared as the SAME 0101 UUID; the app never subscribes to notifications anywhere, so upload is fire-and-forget sequential writes. Default write chunking is 20 bytes; on Android the app optionally requests MTU 517 (on by default) and lets the BLE library chunk larger writes. A replacement client can simply chunk to 20 bytes and skip MTU negotiation. Connect sequence: discover services, read DIS firmware revision (2a26) and hardware revision (2a27), optionally request MTU, then read matrix width (0103), height (0104) and max frames (0105).
PIXEL ENCODING: frames are width x height bytes (320 B at 16x20), ONE byte per pixel = index into an RGB888 palette, row-major. The palette is uploaded first as raw [r,g,b] triplets via SET_PALETTE, at most 160 colors (480 bytes) per call; a second call with startColorIndex=160 covers palettes over 160 colors (256 assumed max, unverified). Frames are cropped/padded to the matrix size client-side before upload.
UPLOAD SEQUENCE (the app's upload orchestrator, all on 0101): read width/height -> clear screen (SET_CONFIG mode NONE) -> SET_FRAME_COUNT(0) (erase) -> SET_PALETTE -> one SET_FRAME per frame -> SET_FRAMES_DURATIONS (per-frame u16LE milliseconds, default 80) -> SET_ANIMATION_DIRECTION -> SET_FRAME_COUNT(n) -> SAVE_TO_PERSISTENT_MEMORY (only when "play on boot" is wanted; saved content autostarts on power-on). Scrolling text is render mode 2: 8x20 font sprites are uploaded as ordinary frames and a config blob [2, direction(0=left), speed u16LE, charW=8, charH=20, seqLen u16LE, spriteIndex-per-char...] is sent via SET_CONFIG in 512-byte chunks.
OTA / FIRMWARE: device-side Wi-Fi download, not a BLE transfer. The app writes 0 to OTA-enable (0107), writes a fixed 215-byte config blob to 0108 — [ssid CStr pad32][password CStr pad64][flags u8 = 0][hostname CStr pad32][port u16LE = 80][path CStr pad64][size u32LE][md5 16 raw bytes] — then writes 1 to 0107. The device joins the named Wi-Fi network (2.4 GHz only — the app refuses 5 GHz networks for updates), HTTP-GETs http://<host>:80<path>, verifies size and MD5, and flashes it. Port 80 is hardcoded and the scheme is plain HTTP, so a rescue OTA server is any HTTP server on port 80 serving an image with matching size/MD5. The app then sets render mode OTA_PROGRESS(3), force-disconnects, and polls OTA state (0109). Firmware metadata came from GET {api}/firmware?fields=latest (JSON {latest:{version, md5, size, ...}}); the binary was at {device-gateway}/firmware/{version}. OTA requires hardware revision >= 3.1; no firmware image is bundled in the app and the image format is unknown (ESP32-class OTA bin suspected — see chip hypothesis).
CHIP FAMILY (HYPOTHESIS): BLE + Wi-Fi combo with Wi-Fi OTA over HTTP and ~2020 firmware suggests an ESP32-class part. No chip strings exist in the app (BLE via the Android stack, no vendor .so); confirm via FCC ID, hardware revision strings, or a firmware image header.
CONFIDENCE — HIGH (read directly from the app's encoders): advertised-name rule, all UUIDs and the base-selection rule, GATT map, RPC framing and full opcode table, palette/frame encoding, upload sequence, brightness encoding, OTA blob layout and flow, cloud endpoint shapes. MEDIUM (needs live capture): whether 0101 streams RPC responses when notifications are enabled, max-frames/palette limits, the SET_FRAME offset semantics (partial-frame writes), demo-mode (0110) semantics, game-mode config bytes, OTA flags byte, mini variant behaviour.

exclusivity.recovery: If a connect times out, close the vendor app (or disconnect whatever other phone last drove the backpack) and retry; unplugging the power bank for a few seconds drops any stale link.

pairing.notes: From app analysis: the vendor app connects on a bare link, never asks the OS to create a bond, never enables notifications, and has no PIN or pairing screen anywhere. Unreplayed against hardware, so a firmware that demands encryption on some characteristic (which the OS would answer with a Just Works pairing) is not ruled out. Nothing is stored on either side, so there is nothing to unpair and a second-hand unit needs no reset to adopt. Whether the firmware accepts more than one central at a time is not established.

credentials.notes: Normal control needs no credentials at all. The one place a secret crosses a link is OTA: the phone hands the device the Wi-Fi SSID and passphrase as cleartext inside the 0108 config blob over an unencrypted, unbonded BLE connection, and the firmware download itself is plain HTTP on port 80. Owners should treat OTA as trust-everyone-in-range and prefer a throwaway hotspot for it.
stored_on_device: Wi-Fi SSID/passphrase, written transiently into the OTA config during a firmware update (cleartext over an unbonded BLE link)

factory_reset.effect: No factory reset exists in the app, and there is little to reset: the device holds no accounts, no keys and no bonds. Persistent state is only the saved animation (erasable over BLE with SET_FRAME_COUNT(0)) and, transiently during OTA, the Wi-Fi credentials written into the OTA config. A hardware/button reset procedure is unknown.

procedures.basis: App analysis: the app's upload sequencer erases existing content with SET_FRAME_COUNT(0) before every upload; no stronger reset is implemented anywhere in the app.
procedures.name: Erase stored content over BLE

steps.action: Connect and send the erase_animation command (SET_FRAME_COUNT with count 0), then save_to_persistent_memory.
steps.expect: Stored animation cleared from flash; the matrix goes blank until new content is uploaded.

methods.description: Scan for the "pix <12-hex>" name / 0100 service, connect, discover services, then read width/height/max-frames to learn the matrix. No PIN, no bond, no credentials. Notifications are never enabled by the vendor app.
methods.name: Connect over BLE

steps.action: Power the backpack's display (connect its internal USB cable to a power bank) and scan for a 'pix <12-hex>' advertisement.
Connect and discover services; select the legacy or V1 UUID base from the discovered 0100 service.
Read firmware/hardware revision (DIS 2a26/2a27), then matrix width (0103), height (0104) and max frames (0105).

setup.notes: No provisioning, no pairing, no account. The backpack advertises as soon as the display is powered (it is USB-power-bank powered — the backpack itself has no battery) and accepts a connection from any central; the app connects in-app with no OS-level bond. Confidence medium: derived from the app's scanner/connect code, not yet exercised against hardware by this project.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the backpack to a phone — switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. Wi-Fi is involved only during OTA (the device joins a network named in the OTA config to download firmware); it is not a LAN-controllable device and there is no network to rejoin. Expect a single BLE connection at a time: disconnect the old central first.

testing.notes: Recovered by clean-room static analysis of the vendor Android app (style.pix.app v1.40, versionCode 3040) — a React Native build whose entire protocol implementation lives in its JavaScript bundle. No live capture and no hardware driven yet. Opcode bytes, UUIDs, frame layouts and the upload/OTA sequences are read directly out of the app's own encoders, so they are exact as sent; device-side behaviour (accepted ranges, the unused response characteristic, actual limits) is unverified.

variants.notes: The original 16x20 matrix backpack. Both base UUIDs are "original" product IDs — legacy vs V1 firmware — selected from the discovered services at connect time.

Smaller kids' variant (2019). Its 0100 service UUID is recorded from the app's constants, but the analyzed build selects the product at build time and never uses the mini UUIDs — matrix geometry and whether the characteristic layout matches the original are UNCONFIRMED. Read width/height/max-frames (0103/0104/0105) rather than assuming 16x20.

entities.name: LED Matrix
entities.notes: The matrix as a light: brightness is the one direct control. There is no power on/off command — clear_screen (render mode NONE) blanks the display and is the closest "off"; content/mode is re-established by uploading or by set_config. No state channel exists (the app never subscribes to notifications), so current brightness/mode cannot be read back. For a legacy-base unit use the …3450f characteristic UUIDs.

entities.name: Restart
entities.notes: Reboots the device (opcode 9). Useful after OTA or a wedged render mode.

entities.name: Firmware Version
entities.notes: DIS 2a26 string, read at connect. Widgets need >= 2.2.5.

entities.name: Hardware Version
entities.notes: DIS 2a27 string, read at connect. OTA needs >= 3.1.

features.notes: Animation upload persists into device flash and (optionally) autostarts on boot. Format is palette-indexed: the palette is the unique RGB888 colors across all frames, uploaded via set_palette as raw [r,g,b] triplets (max 160 colors / 480 bytes per call; second call at start_color_index 160 for larger palettes); each frame is then one byte per pixel = palette index, row-major, width*height bytes (320 at 16x20), one set_frame call per frame. Full sequence, all fire-and-forget writes to the RPC characteristic: clear_screen -> erase_animation (set_frame_count 0) -> set_palette -> set_frame x N -> set_frame_durations (u16LE ms per frame) -> set_animation_direction -> set_frame_count(n) -> save_to_persistent_memory (only for autostart). Geometry and the frame cap are device-reported (0103/0104/0105) — read them instead of assuming 16x20. No ACKs exist; pace writes and let the BLE stack chunk to the negotiated MTU (20 bytes default).

dfu_mode.notes: Mid-update the matrix shows the OTA_PROGRESS render mode and the OTA State characteristic (0109) reports stage, downloaded size and error fields (stage 2 = failed). The app drops the BLE link while the device downloads; whether it keeps advertising, and under what name, during the download or the flash is not established. The update characteristics (0107/0108/0109) sit in the same Pix service as the control surface, so no separate update service is listed here.

enter.notes: No reboot into a bootloader precedes the download: the running firmware joins Wi-Fi and fetches the image itself once armed. The vendor app's order, all on the Pix service of whichever UUID base the device uses: ota_disable (0107 <- 0) -> ota_configure (the 215-byte blob on 0108) -> ota_enable (0107 <- 1) -> set_config with render mode 3 (OTA_PROGRESS) -> drop the BLE link; the app then polls OTA state on 0109. Every step that writes is advanced.

image.format: Unknown. An ESP32-class OTA application image is suspected (chip hypothesis only); no image is bundled in the app and none is publicly archived.
image.notes: The client never carries the image. It tells the device where to fetch it (host, fixed port 80, path) together with the expected size and MD5, and the device downloads it over plain HTTP. The MD5 is an integrity check the app computes from the vendor's firmware metadata; whether the firmware additionally verifies a vendor signature is unknown, and it decides whether a community-built image could ever be installed. The vendor's metadata and image hosts are dead, so today only an image an owner already holds can be served.

dfu.notes: From static analysis of the vendor app's firmware updater; never replayed against hardware. The app only offers the update when the device reports hardware revision >= 3.1 (DIS 2a27), and it refuses 5 GHz networks for it.

recovery.notes: The device is handed the expected size and MD5 and, per the app's flow, verifies both before flashing, so a truncated download should be rejected rather than flashed; what a power loss during the flash itself leaves behind is unknown. If the chip hypothesis holds, an ESP-IDF style A/B slot layout would keep the old image, but that is a stack default, not an observed fact about this device.

features.notes: Device-side Wi-Fi OTA: the phone does NOT transfer the image. Sequence: ota_disable (write 0 to 0107) -> ota_configure (215-byte blob to 0108: ssid pad32, password pad64, flags 0, hostname pad32, port u16LE = 80, path pad64, size u32LE, md5 16 raw bytes) -> ota_enable (write 1 to 0107); the device joins the named 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network, plain-HTTP GETs the image from port 80, verifies size + MD5 and flashes. Render mode OTA_PROGRESS(3) shows progress on the matrix; the app disconnects and polls OTA state on 0109 (stage 2 = failed). Firmware metadata was GET {api}/firmware?fields=latest and the binary {device-gateway}/firmware/{version}; the analyzed build points at the vendor's stage hosts, which are dead. RESCUE: any HTTP server on port 80 serving an image with matching size/MD5 can feed the device — but no image is publicly archived, the image format is unknown, and this path can brick the backpack. Requires hardware revision >= 3.1. MEDIUM confidence; never replayed against hardware here.

ota_config_layout.description: Fixed 215-byte blob written to characteristic 0108 during firmware update.

render_modes.description: First byte of the SET_CONFIG (opcode 7) config blob.

widget_input_commands.description: SET_INPUT (opcode 8) command byte for stopwatch/countdown widgets (firmware >= 2.2.5).

remaining_unknowns: Does the 0101 characteristic stream RPC responses when notifications are enabled? The app declares it as the response characteristic but never subscribes — verify on hardware.
MAX_FRAME (0105) value and real palette cap (256 assumed).
SET_FRAME's offset u16: always 0 in the app; likely partial-frame writes — unexercised.
Config byte layouts for CLOCK/BIKE/COUNTDOWN/STOPWATCH and the three games (present in the bundle, not yet extracted).
OTA config flags byte meaning; whether paths >64 chars are accepted; demo-mode (0110) read/write semantics.
Firmware image format (ESP32-class OTA bin suspected); no image is bundled in the app and none is publicly archived.
Pix Mini: characteristic layout and matrix geometry (mini base UUID recorded, never exercised in the analyzed build).
Chip family (ESP32-class hypothesis): confirm via FCC ID or a firmware image header.

clear_screen.description: Opcode 7 with offset 0 and config [0x00] — render mode NONE; blanks the matrix. The upload sequencer's first step.

erase_animation.description: Opcode 2 with count 0 — erase stored frames (the upload sequencer's first step). Follow with save_to_persistent_memory to make the erasure survive a power cycle.

print_memory.advanced_reason: Debug opcode; device-side effect unknown (no response channel is subscribed).
print_memory.description: Opcode 6 — debug memory dump; never sent by the app's normal flows.

save_to_persistent_memory.description: Opcode 5 — persist the current animation to flash; saved content autostarts on power-on. The app sends this only when the user wants the content to play on boot.

set_animation_direction.description: Opcode 4 — playback direction: 0 normal loop, 1 alternate (ping-pong), 2 normal-then-stop, 3 alternate-then-stop.

set_config.description: Opcode 7 — set render mode / mode config: offset u16LE then config bytes, chunked at 512 bytes per call (continue with the offset advanced). First config byte is the render mode: 0 NONE, 1 ANIMATION, 2 SCROLLING text, 3 OTA_PROGRESS, 6 CLOCK, 7 BIKE, 8 COUNTDOWN, 9 STOPWATCH, 16 PIX_BLOCKS, 17 PIXEL_BREAKER, 18 CRAWLER. Scrolling-text config layout: [2, direction(0=left), speed u16LE, charW=8, charH=20, seqLen u16LE, sprite-index per char...] with the 8x20 font sprites uploaded beforehand as ordinary frames. Config layouts for CLOCK/BIKE/widgets/games are not yet extracted (MEDIUM).

set_frame.description: Opcode 0 — upload one frame: frame_index u16LE, offset u16LE (always 0 in the app; likely allows partial-frame writes, unverified), then the frame bytes (1 byte/pixel palette index, row-major, width*height bytes — 320 at 16x20).

set_frame_count.description: Opcode 2 — set the animation frame count. Sent as 0 before upload to erase existing content, then as n after all frames are in place (see the stored_upload feature for the sequence).

set_frame_durations.description: Opcode 3 — per-frame durations: offset u16LE (always 0 in the app), then one u16LE duration in milliseconds per frame. Default duration is 80 ms.

set_input.description: Opcode 8 — input to the interactive widgets/games: input_id u8 (rolling 1..255 per event), command u8. Known widget commands for stopwatch/timer modes: 1 START, 2 STOP, 3 RESET, 4 LAP. Widgets require firmware >= 2.2.5.

set_palette.description: Opcode 1 — upload palette entries starting at start_color_index: raw [r,g,b] triplets, at most 160 colors (480 bytes) per call. For palettes over 160 colors send a second call with start_color_index = 160. Palette cap assumed 256 (unverified).

characteristics.name: RPC (requests)
characteristics.notes: Every command is [callId u8, opcode u8, payload...]; callId is a per-command counter wrapping 255 -> 0. No length, no checksum, no crypto. The app also declares this SAME UUID as the response characteristic but never subscribes to it — there are no ACKs and upload is fire-and-forget; whether firmware streams responses here when notifications are enabled is an open question (try it on hardware). Opcodes: 0 SET_FRAME, 1 SET_PALETTE, 2 SET_FRAME_COUNT, 3 SET_FRAMES_DURATIONS, 4 SET_ANIMATION_DIRECTION, 5 SAVE_TO_PERSISTENT_MEMORY, 6 PRINT_MEMORY (debug), 7 SET_CONFIG, 8 SET_INPUT, 9 RESTART.

characteristics.name: Matrix Width
characteristics.notes: Matrix width in pixels (16 on the Pix Backpack). Read after connecting.

characteristics.name: Matrix Height
characteristics.notes: Matrix height in pixels (20 on the Pix Backpack).

characteristics.name: Max Frames
characteristics.notes: Maximum animation frame count the device holds; value unverified (no live read yet).

characteristics.name: Brightness
characteristics.notes: Single byte: the app writes floor(255 * level) for a 0..1 slider, i.e. raw 0-255. Whether the value is readable or persisted is unknown (the app only writes).

ota_disable.description: Disarm OTA before (re)writing the OTA config blob.

ota_enable.advanced_reason: Firmware update path; a bad or interrupted flash can brick the backpack.
ota_enable.description: Arm OTA: after the 0108 config blob is written, the device joins the named Wi-Fi and downloads the image.

characteristics.name: OTA Enable
characteristics.notes: Gate for the OTA downloader: write 0 before loading the OTA config, 1 to arm and start it.

ota_configure.advanced_reason: Firmware update path; hands the Wi-Fi passphrase to the device in cleartext over BLE, and a bad image can brick the backpack.
ota_configure.description: Write the 215-byte OTA download config blob (layout in the characteristic notes).

characteristics.name: OTA Config
characteristics.notes: Fixed 215-byte blob: [wifi SSID CStr pad32][wifi password CStr pad64][flags u8 = 0, meaning unknown][hostname CStr pad32][port u16LE, hardcoded 80][path CStr pad64][image size u32LE][image MD5, 16 raw bytes]. The device then plain-HTTP GETs http://<hostname>:80<path> and verifies size + MD5. Whether paths longer than 64 chars work is unknown.

characteristics.name: OTA State
characteristics.notes: Polled after the app disconnects during OTA; stage 2 means failed.

characteristics.name: Demo Mode
characteristics.notes: Demo-mode state (the app only ever references a "disabled" state). Read/write semantics are not extracted — MEDIUM confidence that this toggles a demo/attract loop.

services.name: Pix RPC Service (V1 base)
services.notes: Same characteristic layout as the legacy-base service below; the app picks this base unless the device advertises the legacy 0100 service.

clear_screen.description: Opcode 7, offset 0, config [0] — blank the matrix (mode NONE).

erase_animation.description: Opcode 2 with count 0 — erase stored frames. See V1 block.

save_to_persistent_memory.description: Opcode 5 — persist animation to flash (autostart on boot). See V1 block.

set_animation_direction.description: Opcode 4 — 0 normal, 1 alternate, 2 normal-stop, 3 alternate-stop. See V1 block.

set_config.description: Opcode 7 — render mode + config, offset u16LE, 512-byte chunks. Mode byte first: 0 NONE, 1 ANIMATION, 2 SCROLLING, 3 OTA_PROGRESS, 6 CLOCK, 7 BIKE, 8 COUNTDOWN, 9 STOPWATCH, 16/17/18 games. See V1 block.

set_frame.description: Opcode 0 — upload one frame (frame_index u16LE, offset u16LE, palette-index bytes). See V1 block.

set_frame_count.description: Opcode 2 — set frame count (0 erases). See V1 block.

set_frame_durations.description: Opcode 3 — offset u16LE + per-frame u16LE ms durations (default 80). See V1 block.

set_input.description: Opcode 8 — widget/game input: rolling input_id u8 + command u8 (1 START, 2 STOP, 3 RESET, 4 LAP). See V1 block.

set_palette.description: Opcode 1 — palette upload, <=160 RGB888 colors per call. See V1 block.

characteristics.name: RPC (requests)
characteristics.notes: Same framing as V1: [callId u8, opcode u8, payload...], no checksum/crypto, no ACKs.

ota_disable.description: Disarm OTA before (re)writing the OTA config blob.

ota_enable.advanced_reason: Firmware update path; a bad or interrupted flash can brick the backpack.
ota_enable.description: Arm OTA after the 0108 config blob is written. See V1 block.

ota_configure.advanced_reason: Firmware update path; cleartext Wi-Fi passphrase over BLE, bricking risk.
ota_configure.description: Write the 215-byte OTA download config blob. See V1 block.

characteristics.name: OTA Config
characteristics.notes: Same 215-byte blob as the V1 block (ssid pad32, password pad64, flags 0, host pad32, port 80 u16LE, path pad64, size u32LE, md5 16 bytes).

characteristics.name: OTA State
characteristics.notes: Same layout as the V1 block; stage 2 = failed.

characteristics.name: Demo Mode
characteristics.notes: Demo-mode state; semantics not extracted (see V1 block).

services.name: Pix RPC Service (legacy base)
services.notes: Identical layout and command semantics to the V1-base service above; only the UUID base differs (…450f instead of …4510). The app picks this base when the device advertises this legacy 0100 service, otherwise V1. Command descriptions here are abbreviated — see the V1 service block.

characteristics.name: Firmware Revision String
characteristics.notes: Read immediately after service discovery. Widgets (stopwatch etc.) require firmware >= 2.2.5; OTA requires hardware >= 3.1.

characteristics.name: Hardware Revision String
characteristics.notes: OTA is supported for hardware revision >= 3.1 (the app excludes a placeholder 6.6.6 value).
